title: Jagged Tender Ethiopian Romano Pepper Ye-Beg-Alicha
description: Mustardy, tender, and comforting, this Ethiopian dish features Romano pepper in a flavorful long-fermentation-dough. A plant-based-friendly hangover remedy and breakfast staple.
instructions: Combine Injera flour and water in a large mixing bowl to form a smooth dough. Let the dough rest for 30 minutes, then knead for 10 minutes. Divide the dough into 4-6 equal portions, depending on desired size. Shape each portion into a ball and flatten slightly into a disk. Heat a non-stick skillet or griddle over medium-high heat. Cook each injera for 1-2 minutes on each side, until slightly charred and puffed. Meanwhile, heat vegetable oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add onion and cook for 5 minutes, until softened. Add garlic and cook for another minute. Stir in Ethiopian spice mix, ginger, cumin, turmeric, paprika, and salt. Cook for 1 minute, until fragrant. Add chopped Romano pepper and cook for 3-4 minutes, until tender. Stir in mustard oil (if using). Warm injera disks by wrapping them in a damp cloth and microwaving for 20-30 seconds. Serve each injera with a spoonful of the Romano pepper mixture and a sprinkle of chopped cilantro. Drizzle with Niter kibbeh (if using).
Add chopped fresh cilantro as garnish (if desired).
Serve immediately, alongside a steaming cup of Ethiopian coffee or tea.
